title: PGA Tour establishes 2028 membership rules: career earnings exemption, no LIV pathway
dek: The PGA Tour has established Championship Series and Challenger Series eligibility rules for 2028, creating a career earnings exemption for top earners but blocking any pathway for LIV returnees currently banned from competition.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: The PGA Tour's 2028 structure offers a career money exemption to the top 50 earners in PGA Tour history, but explicitly requires 15 or more PGA Tour events in 2027 to use it, locking out LIV players including Phil Mickelson, Dustin Johnson, and Jon Rahm.
bottom_line: The PGA Tour's 2028 structure codifies meritocracy and locks out LIV returnees through a 15-event-in-2027 requirement that currently excludes all banned players, but the Tour's repeated emphasis on "refined and evolved" rules suggests the framework may shift if LIV's bankruptcy proceedings or market conditions change before 2027. The number of DP World Tour cards available for Championship Series membership remains unset, leaving cross-tour access routes undetermined.
body:
The PGA Tour on September 15 outlined eligibility criteria for its restructured 2028 competition model, establishing a Championship Series and Challenger Series with purses starting at $20 million and $4 million respectively, per Front Office Sports. The system includes a career earnings exemption for top earners but explicitly forecloses any route for LIV players currently banned from the Tour.
The Championship Series will comprise 114 members in 2028, with 120-player fields, according to CBS Sports. The top 90 performers from the prior season will earn automatic membership, with 20 additional players promoted from the Challenger Series, per Front Office Sports. Three spots will be available through a fall "last-chance" series and one through the PGA Tour University program. Twenty Championship Series members will be relegated annually.
Points will determine standing within the Championship Series. According to CBS Sports, the winner of qualifying Championship Series tournaments will earn 300 points, the 10th-place finisher 100 points, and the 65th-place finisher 30 points, with points awarded to the top 65 finishers. The Challenger Series points list will be finalized on November 16, per CBS Sports.
The career money exemption targets established players in decline. Per Front Office Sports, players ranking in the top 50 of PGA Tour all-time career earnings may use a one-time exemption to claim Championship Series status if they lose standing, provided they held membership the prior season. For the inaugural 2028 season, eligibility requires playing 15 or more PGA Tour events in 2027.
Front Office Sports identified potential beneficiaries: Jordan Spieth (No. 10 on the career money list), Brooks Koepka (No. 26), Justin Rose (No. 4), Adam Scott (No. 5), Matt Kuchar (No. 14), Jason Day (No. 12), Tony Finau (No. 23), and Billy Horschel (No. 35). However, the requirement to play 15 PGA Tour events in 2027 creates a practical barrier for LIV players.
PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp reaffirmed the organization's stance on LIV. "In terms of where we are today, we are not currently contemplating a returning-member program like the one you saw in January," Rolapp stated, per Front Office Sports. He added: "There are really three things when it comes to anyone who wants to compete on the PGA Tour. One, the PGA Tour is built on meritocracy. Every player, whether they are a member or want to become one, must earn their place. Two, we are a membership organisation; we have rules and those rules exist for lots of reasons, including fairness and competitive balance. Rules matter, and they must be enforced. Which brings me to No 3, accountability and discipline."
Chief competitions officer Tyler Dennis described the career money exemption as rewarding achievement. "It's an important feature of the overall eligibility system that rewards a player who's had an incredible career," Dennis said, per Front Office Sports. He added that the Tour has "put some guardrails around" the system. Rolapp noted the framework remains flexible: guidelines for 2027 will be unique, with "refined and evolved" permanent criteria introduced in 2028.
Cross-tour movement remains unresolved. Rolapp stated: "We have not determined what the DP World Tour cards will be, as of yet. That's under discussion. I don't see any scenarios where there's no Championship Series cards," per the Guardian. Rory McIlroy expressed skepticism about DP World Tour players descending to the Challenger Series. "I don't see any reason why a DP World Tour player would go to the Challenger Series. I don't see that as an upward move in your career. I see it as a very lateral move," McIlroy said, per the Guardian.
